punchline: In Harlem, kids spent three nights painting a subway car, and a crew painted it over with rollers.
thirty_sec: In the 1980s New York subway director David Gunn started with graffiti, though advisers said the system had bigger problems. A cleaned car was never allowed to be vandalised again. Later William Bratton went after fare-beating. Gladwell calls this Broken Windows thinking the most intriguing candidate for why crime fell, though he lists other explanations.
